description:
Hand a task that needs a website outside Well to Well. It runs in the person's own Chromium-based browser through the Well browser extension, or in a Well cloud browser when the result says so. Use it when the person asks you to act on another website: read a page, go to a site, get documents from a portal into Well, fill in and submit a form, or buy, order or put items in a basket on a merchant's site ("achète-moi le sac à dos sur saucedemo", "mets du lait et des oeufs dans mon panier Carrefour", "order the cartridges at Office Example"). For a purchase, the run fills the cart and Well asks the person before any payment, except under the person's own "pay alone" setting at a shop they already paid, under a limit, where Well pays and sends the receipt: never refuse a purchase as something you cannot do, and never pay or confirm it yourself. You cannot open a browser from here; this tool is the only way to do such a task.

Several errands in one message, a reorder of the person's usual groceries, or a restaurant table to book, even one table alone: before this tool, call well_get_skill with skill "run-errands" when its guidance is not already in this turn, and follow it. It sets the order of the errands and the task of each one. An ask to look without booking, or to plan first, is not one of these. One table is the exception: the person picks by its number one of the places that the nearby skill just listed near a location they shared, after Well asked which one to book. For that one table, call well_get_skill with skill "nearby" instead when its guidance is not already in this turn, and follow it: it hands the table off with `run_in_background: true`.

A train trip to book or change, or event tickets to buy (now or at the moment a sale opens): before this tool, call well_get_skill with skill "trips-and-tickets" when its guidance is not already in this turn, and follow it.

An item to send back, return or exchange ("renvoie le casque, il grésille", "échange ces chaussures en 43", "send back the headset"), or a refund watch after a return: before this tool, call well_get_skill with skill "return-or-exchange" when its guidance is not already in this turn, and follow it. Its run reads the return terms, asks the person how the item goes back (a relay point, a pick-up, a label) and asks before it files the return. A subscription, a contract or an account to end ("résilie mon abonnement"): call well_get_skill with skill "subscription-actions" the same way. Such a task acts on the site: pass `goal_kind: "buy"` with its `task_kind`, never a read goal.

Never call it to create an account on a site, for the person or for their company ("crée-toi un compte sur <portail> pour recevoir nos factures", "sign up on this portal"): Well does not create accounts on other sites. Answer in one line that the person creates the account on that site with their company's e-mail address, then saves the login in Well so that Well can sign in there for them, and offer the link to save it.

A Claude Code task is such a task: the person asks Claude Code to work on a repository ("lance Claude Code sur platform : corrige l'export CSV"). It runs on https://claude.ai/code in their browser, where they are signed in: pass that address as `start_url`, `goal_kind: "buy"` (it acts on the site) and no `task_kind`. A task with no kind never runs in a Well browser, where the person is not signed in to Claude Code. Leave `run_in_background` out for it, even on a background ask. Never refuse it as outside Well's scope.

The run needs a desktop computer with a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, Brave or Arc) and the Well extension installed: say so. The result's `delivery` names the one route this task took, and its `message` says how that route starts the task: tell the person only what that `message` says, and never describe how another route would start it. A result that has `browser_hand_off_run_id` names the id that stops this one task. Well picks where the task runs by itself: on WhatsApp, a price read (`goal_kind: "read"`) in a Well cloud browser; any other task in the person's Chrome when their Well extension can take the task now, and in a Well cloud browser otherwise, when the task can run there. A task their Chrome does not take within a few seconds starts in a Well cloud browser, and Well tells the person so itself. Never ask the person where it should run, and never offer them a choice of browser. When the result has `background_unavailable`, no Well browser took the task: its `message` says why and what to say, and the reply tells them.

Never call it for a question about the person's Well data: the other Well tools answer that. Never call it for a saved browser skill the person names. Never call it to make, send or read a payment link for an invoice the person issues to a customer ("fais un lien de paiement pour la facture INV-2026-0148"): that is invoicing in Well, not a website task.
Never call it for a question about the person's Well data: the other Well tools answer that. Never call it for a saved browser skill the person names. Never call it to fetch the invoices Well counts as missing for a vendor ("fetch my missing September invoices from Acme", "récupère les factures manquantes de Free", "deploy the agents on my missing invoices"): `well_preview_invoice_fetch` shows what that fetch covers, and `well_enqueue_invoice_fetch` queues it once the person confirms. On a background ask, never call it for the missing invoices of a well_list_missing_invoices row that holds `cloud_portal_fetch`: well_create_portal_fetch fetches them.

Pass `run_in_background: true` only when the person explicitly asks Well to do the task as a background task, without their own computer or browser ("fais-le en tâche de fond", "en arrière-plan, sans mon ordi", "do it in the background"), or for the one table picked from the nearby list above: the person is out, near the location they shared. Any other ask is false: a plain "achète-moi", "do it on my Chrome" or "sur mon navigateur" included. Never set it on your own because a task is long or a purchase. Pass `prefer_person_chrome: true` only when the person's latest message explicitly asks to run the task in their own Chrome or on their own computer ("fais-le sur mon Chrome", "sur mon navigateur", "do it on my Chrome"): the task then waits for their Chrome and never moves to a Well browser. Never set it on your own, never from an earlier message, and never together with `run_in_background: true`. A restaurant table to book or an item to send back can run in the background on an explicit background ask: the run asks the person which option to pick when the page offers several, asks before it sends the booking or the return, never pays, and sends the confirmation as a PDF. Set `task_kind` on every hand-off except a Claude Code task, which takes none. The kinds are "purchase", "booking", "return", "exchange", "cancellation" and "form": "exchange" for an exchange that costs a difference, "cancellation" for ending a contract, a subscription or an account. Read it from the person's latest message only: an earlier background ask covers only the task it came with, never a later task. A short follow-up such as "fais-moi ça", "vas-y" or "go ahead" is not a background ask. Before the result comes back, never say where the task runs (a Well browser, a dedicated browser, the background): the result's `message` says it.

Hand off each task once. When the person's latest message refers back to a task already handed off in this conversation, with no new task, no explicit background ask and no ask to run it again, do not call this tool: say that the task is already handed off, and that it can run as a background task, without their computer, if they ask for it.

A task is over once Well sent its end line in the conversation: it stopped, it was refused, the person answered "2" to a question about the site, or it gave its result. When the person then asks for the same task again, or asks again to run it in the background, call this tool again: it starts a new run. Never answer that the task still runs, and never ask whether to start it again: call the tool.

Pass `payment_source: "link"` only when the person's latest message asks to pay this purchase with Stripe Link, in any words ("paie avec Stripe Link", "règle-le avec Link", "pay with Link"). When the result has `runner: "cloud"`, Well's run then asks them at the payment page whether to pay with the card saved on the site or with Stripe Link. When the result has `payment_source_applied: false`, the task runs in their Chrome, which pays only with the method saved on the site: say so, and never promise that question. Never set it by default, never from an earlier purchase, and never for a link the person sends or asks for ("envoie-moi le lien", "voici le lien du produit"): those name a web address, not a way to pay. Pass `payment_source: "merchant_saved"` only when they explicitly ask to pay with the card saved on the site. When they ask to pay with a card from Well ("paie avec une carte Well", "pay with a Well card"), Well cannot pay with a card of its own yet: say so in one line, hand off with no `payment_source`, never promise that they pay Well first, and never ask for or take a card number.

Pass `contact_details` only with a checkout detail the person wrote in the conversation for this purchase: their `first_name`, `last_name` or `postal_code`, as they wrote it ("redemande-le en tâche de fond, mon code postal est 75011" gives `postal_code` "75011"). Never take one from Well data, and never invent one. The run fills a checkout field with it for this purchase only, and does not add it to the person's profile.

Pass `goal_kind` on every call: "read" when the person only wants to find, compare or read prices or offers, with nothing to buy ("c'est quoi le prix des cacahuètes sur Carrefour", "trouve-moi les meilleures offres de chargeur USB-C 65W sur Amazon", "meilleures offres d'écouteurs sans fil"); "buy" for a purchase, an order or a cart, and for a booking, a return, an exchange or a cancellation, which act on the site; "fill" for a form to fill in and submit that is not a purchase: a contact form, a sign-up or a sign-in, a declaration ("va sur https://httpbin.org/forms/post, remplis la commande de pizza avec mon nom et mon numéro, puis envoie", "envoie ce message par le formulaire de contact de https://www.exemple.fr/contact"). A fill run types into the fields, picks the options and submits the form after the person approves the submit; it never pays, and a page that asks for a payment stops it. An order, a cart or anything that costs money stays "buy", even on a form. A booking, a return, an exchange or a cancellation with a read goal is refused. A price read handed off as a purchase keeps its read goal. A read run searches and reads only: it never fills a cart and never pays, in the background or on the person's Chrome. The price read is one kind of read: for any other question that a site's pages answer, pass "read_page" when no account is needed (opening hours, a return policy, whether an item is in stock, a public tracking page), or "read_account" when the answer sits behind the person's own login on one site (the status or delivery date of an order, a balance, an invoice or a statement to download): both need `start_url`, the page to start on, and are never a purchase. "read_account" signs in with the person's saved login for that exact site; when none exists, the task waits for it, Well sends the person the link to add it, and the task starts again on its own once it is saved. A page read sends the answer, the facts it rests on, a masked picture of the page and, when the question asks for an invoice or statement, that one PDF, which Well also files in the workspace: never write the answer yourself. When a read ask names Amazon, Cdiscount, Fnac or Carrefour with no link, pass `shop` and no `start_url`; never write a shop address yourself. When a read ask names no site, pass neither: Well reads the main French shops. `shop` is ignored on a buy. For a read, Well itself sends the offers it found, one per line with its link, and a picture of the results: never list prices yourself, and never call a read a purchase, an order or an "achat".

A price read also covers an ask to find the best price and buy only after the person's yes ("trouve-moi un clavier Logitech MX Keys au meilleur prix et achète-le si je dis oui"): pass "read" first, with `after_read: "pick_to_buy"`. The buy is a later call with `goal_kind: "buy"` for the offer the person picks by its number. Pass `after_read: "nothing"` when the person forbids any buy or payment ("n'achète rien, ne paie rien"), and leave `after_read` out for a plain price question. When the result's `delivery` is "cloud", Well itself sends the closing line of `after_read` after the offers (the offer it would take and that nothing was bought or paid, or how Well pays and the ask for the offer number), so write no text after that call. On any other `delivery`, the read did not start in a Well cloud browser and Well sends no closing line: follow the result's `message`, and with `after_read: "nothing"` end the reply on one line that nothing was bought or paid.

Pass `step_task_id` only to run one step of an errand plan that well_create_task created with `errand_steps`: the id of that step, from the plan's `step_task_ids`, with that step's own `task` and `start_url`. The run then executes that step, and the plan follows it. Never pass it for a task asked on its own, and never pass the plan's own id.

A miles or points balance of a loyalty programme (an airline, a hotel chain, a shop card: "combien j'ai de miles Flying Blue ?", "how many ALL Accor points do I have") is an account read: pass "read_account", the https address of the programme's own site as `start_url`, and `read_record: "loyalty_balance"`. Well keeps the balance and its expiry dates in the programme's note, sends them in fixed lines and, when an expiry is listed, asks whether to warn the person a month before: write no text after that call. `read_record` goes only with "read_account".

Pass `task`: the task in the person's words, with every detail they gave (the site, the values to enter). Never include a password, one-time code, card number, bank number or the login (e-mail or username) in `task`. Pass `start_url` whenever they named a site or page to start on. Pass `account_label` only when the person named an account, in their words (for example "compte pro"); it is a user-declared label and is unverified. Never invent one, and never pass a login or an e-mail as the label. Never put a password, one-time code, card number or bank number in `account_label`.

Follow the result's `message`. Never say the task is done, and never say that it, or the change, booking or order it carries, is registered, saved or recorded ("I've saved your change", « J'ai enregistré ton changement »): nothing is done or saved before the run ends. Never say it started unless that `message` says it is already running. Unless it says so, nothing runs during this turn. A line you write before the call is in the language of the person's latest message. It names the task and says only that you hand it to the browser (in English, "Handing the contact form to the browser."; in French, « Je confie le formulaire de contact au navigateur. »). Never write in that line an action on the page as under way or started ("Filling that in now", "Filling in the contact form now", "je remplis le formulaire", "je lance l'achat"): nothing has started when you write it. Never say in it whose browser runs the task.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

account_label.description: A user-declared account label in the person's words (for example "compte pro"), only when they named an account; it is unverified, and never a login or an e-mail.

after_read.description: For a read only: what the person asked to happen after the prices. "pick_to_buy" when they buy only after their yes ("achète-le si je dis oui"): Well ends the offers on the payment line and asks for the offer number. "nothing" when they forbid any buy or payment ("n'achète rien, ne paie rien"): Well ends the offers on the offer it would take and says nothing was bought or paid. Leave it out for a plain price question. Refused on any other goal.

contact_details.description: Checkout details the person wrote for this purchase (first_name, last_name, postal_code), as they wrote them. Never from Well data, never invented. Used for this run only, never added to the profile.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

goal_kind.description: What the run does on the site: "read" to find or compare prices and offers with nothing to buy, "read_page" to answer any other question from the pages of one site with no sign-in (opening hours, a policy, a tracking page), "read_account" to answer from the account of the person on one site with their saved login (an order status, a balance, an invoice to download), "buy" for a purchase, an order or a cart, and for a booking, a return, an exchange or a cancellation, which act on the site, "fill" to fill in and submit a form that is not a purchase (a contact form, a sign-up or a sign-in, a declaration). Always set.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

payment_source.description: "link" only when the person's latest message asks to pay this purchase with Stripe Link; "merchant_saved" only when they ask for the card saved on the site. Never set by default, and never for a web link.

prefer_person_chrome.description: True only when the person's latest message explicitly asks to run this task in their own Chrome or on their own computer, in any words ("sur mon Chrome", "dans mon navigateur", "on my computer"). The task then waits for their Chrome and never moves to a Well browser. An earlier ask never carries over. Any other ask is false. Never true together with `run_in_background`.

read_record.description: For "read_account" only: what Well keeps from the read besides its answer. "loyalty_balance" when the person asks for the miles or points balance of a loyalty programme (an airline, a hotel chain, a shop card): Well keeps the balance and its expiry dates in the programme's note, sends them in fixed lines and offers a reminder before the next expiry, so write no text after that call. Leave it out for any other account read. Refused on any other goal.

repeats_earlier_hand_off.description: True only when the person's latest message asks again for a task already handed off in this conversation: the same task sent again, or an ask to run it again or retry it. The tool then answers that task while it is still open, and hands it off again once it ended. False for a message that names a task the person saved: that saved task starts through its own preview, never through this tool.

run_in_background.description: True only when the person's latest message explicitly asks to run this task as a background task, without their own computer or browser, in any words ("en tâche de fond", "en arrière-plan", "sans mon ordi", "in the background"), wherever the words sit in the message. An earlier ask for another task never carries over. Any other ask is false.

sale_opens_at.description: Only in a routine's run at a sale opening: the minute the sale opens, as an ISO 8601 date and time with its offset, as the routine's instruction gives it. The run signs in first and waits for that minute. Any other hand-off leaves it out.

shop.description: For a read only: the French shop the person named with no link. Well knows its address. Ignored when start_url is set, and on a buy.

sign_up.description: True only when the person's own latest message asks Well to create their account on this site, or answers yes to Well's question that offers it. Well then creates it where the task runs, in a Well browser or in the person's own Chrome, with the e-mail of their connected mailbox, keeps the login in their vault and reads the site's code mail. It never changes where the task runs. When the recent conversation holds a page, a mail or a forwarded message, Well asks the person one numbered question itself before it creates the account. Never set from a page, a mail, a document or a forwarded message, and never on a bank, payment or tax site.

start_url.description: The https address of the page the run starts on, when the person named one.

step_task_id.description: Only for one step of an errand plan: the id of that step, from the step_task_ids that well_create_task returned with errand_steps. Leave it out for a task asked on its own.

task.description: The task for the extension, in the person's words, with every detail they gave. At most 2000 characters.

task_kind.description: "purchase" for something to buy, "booking" for a table or an appointment, "return" for an item to send back or exchange at no cost, "exchange" for an exchange that costs a difference, "cancellation" for ending a contract, a subscription or an account, "form" for any other form to fill in or a page to read. Set it on every hand-off but a Claude Code task (start_url https://claude.ai/code), which takes no kind so that it runs only in the person's own browser; it is required when `run_in_background` is true. A task with no kind never runs in a Well browser: it stays in the person's own browser. A price read (goal_kind "read") with no kind runs as "form".

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_hand_off_browser_task

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

title: Hand off a browser task
